DIFC.rationale: Administrative appointment of 4 additional Small Claims Tribunal members. NOT an adjudicative ruling — it is a *rule-making* / appointment act by the Chief Justice in administrative capacity. P4=2 because this is exactly the separation-of-powers moment: the Chief Justice sitting as administrator authorises the bench, then sits separately when adjudicating cases brought to it. P3=0 (no parties), P6=0 (administrative). Including this in the first-pass set is intentional — it shows the corpus contains rule-making acts AND adjudicative acts, and the protocol must distinguish them.

USD 45,000 awarded as claimed; defendant filed no submissions. P3=1 because while opposing party had opportunity, none was taken — partial trace. P2=2 because in absence of opposition, the rule reduces to 'is the amount reasonable on its face' which is more deterministic than contested cases.

Indemnity-basis costs reduced from AED 85,417.50 to AED 80,000. P3=1 because Second Defendant failed to file written submissions despite opportunity. Court reasons: 27 hours = 3 man-days; reduction for 'duplication of work'. Bounded discretion under indemnity standard, parallel to ENF 271/2025.

ADGM.rationale: Anti-suit injunction case (anonymised). Costs allocation following discontinuance. PR1=1 because parties are anonymised — but this is a structural protection, not an absence of identity (court has full identity, public does not). PR3 cites both ADGM Court Procedure Rules 2016 Rule 172(1) presumption + Section 49 of Courts Regulations broad discretion. Demonstrates the ADGM tribunal's facility with English-law costs jurisprudence.
